adoption.notes: Implements the Producer Time members and the action_log record members in the sensor_history and action_log exports and the Tier 3 request, and vendors this version's export-rows corpus. It does not claim this version and pages action_log by count. It enforces neither Payload Size nor Payload Volume. It answers an export request whose envelope is not verified with a signed error response, auth_failed or internal_error, which this version forbids. From 97649a76 it keeps each replay key until its envelope is stale or replay_ttl_ms from receipt, whichever is later, and persists the keys while persistent_replay_cache is true, its default, warming at most its capacity of them at a start and falling back to memory alone when the store fails; it refuses a fresh envelope as replay_detected when full, un-records an inbound evidence key when its executor is saturated, which this version forbids, keeps no replay floor and refuses nothing as before_replay_floor. It checks freshness before the signature, so a forged stale envelope is counted as stale_timestamp.

notes: Created by the baseline audit of gateway-api/v1 as the destination of its three semantic post-freeze hunks: the gateway serves only configured devices, the reasoning response carries a required `device_id` and the runtime refuses an invalid `action_tier`, and an explicit `escalate_to: gateway` returns a gateway-unavailable result instead of falling back. The text is v1's as it stood on main before the audit removed those edits from v1; v1 also keeps the additive families (runtime node heartbeat, enrichment, evidence carriage, exports) as they stood. This version carries their successors where runtime-health/v4 changes them: the runtime node heartbeat gains the `critical` status, the enlarged `degradation_reasons` vocabulary and its validation steps, and the `health` export becomes the remote health projection. The runtime shipped the response rule in v1.0.0 and will be recorded here once it claims this version. Amended in place while amendable: sensor readings carry `producer_time`, so a receipt sent in `timestamp` is never read as a measurement, and `action_log` rows carry `record_kind`, `record_key` and `contributed_to` in a stable page order. Payload Size bounds every topic's payload length before any parse, and Payload Volume bounds each receiver's processing rate and state; the maxima count `device_id` at the bound runtime-config/v2 declares and `request_id` at 128 characters, every required reply fits the 4096-byte floor, and an inbound evidence message is published in canonical form. No implementation enforces either yet. Export Auth Envelope defines the export envelope: a runtime does not answer an export request whose envelope is not verified, and a gateway drops an unverified export response and bounds its wait for every export request, which it adopts first. Neither side enforces this yet. Envelope Freshness and Replay keeps each replay key until its envelope is stale, with replay_ttl_ms only a lower bound, and adds a replay floor: every dropped key raises it past that envelope's signing time, every start raises it to the start clock, and an envelope signed below it is refused as before_replay_floor. Every sender signs each attempt afresh. The runtime keeps keys until stale on its main branch and keeps no floor yet. The gateway keeps each key a fixed five minutes from receipt, in memory, under a fixed five-minute skew, so an envelope signed at the future edge can be replayed between five and ten minutes after receipt; it names stale and future alike and keeps no floor.
